angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 841,797 km at 129.77 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.7059 +/- 0.0170 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 129.77 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.21 +/- 0.036 solar radii from Ranshaw et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-232 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260909077R/abstract): 841,797 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.121 +/- 0.063 solar masses from Ranshaw et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-232 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260909077R/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6100 +/- 100 K from Ranshaw et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-232 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260909077R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ranshaw et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-232 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260909077R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-232.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.322, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
